column3: Accept a pleasant or worthwhile aspect of waiting or eating, or a related constructive response. A brief sign of enjoyment is enough; do not require an explanation of why it is positive.
column4: 기다리는 동안 같이 온 사람과 여유롭게 이야기할 수 있었어.
column5: The wait gave us time to chat without rushing.
column6: 待つ間に、一緒に来た人とゆっくり話せた。

column3: Accept enjoyment, company, participating, trying again or another constructive take on playing with friends. Winning or an explicit contrast with losing is not required.
column4: 승패와 별개로 친구들과 웃으며 시간을 보낸 게 좋았어.
column5: Even without winning, laughing with my friends was fun.
column6: 勝てなくても、友達と笑って過ごせたのが楽しかった。

column3: Accept rest, bodily needs, taking things slowly or a manageable way to continue after sleeping late. No need to explain both the benefit and the delayed cleaning.
column4: 청소는 늦어졌지만 몸이 필요했던 잠을 푹 잤어.
column5: Cleaning is delayed, but I got the rest my body needed.
column6: 掃除は遅れたけれど、体に必要な睡眠を取れた。

column3: Accept any reasonable upside or constructive take on making food at home. Everyday satisfaction, convenience or saving money is enough.
column4: 재료를 직접 골라서 내 입맛에 맞게 먹을 수 있었어.
column5: I could choose the ingredients and make it to my taste.
column6: 材料を自分で選び、好みの味にできた。

column3: Accept a reasonable upside or helpful response to rain near home. Simply being glad to be nearby or able to get an umbrella is enough.
column4: 멀리 나가기 전에 비가 와서 우산을 챙길 수 있어 다행이야.
column5: Luckily, the rain started while I could still go back for an umbrella.
column6: 遠くへ行く前に雨が降ったから、傘を取りに戻れてよかった。

column3: Accept relief that some work remains, that the loss is limited, or a manageable way to resume. Describing the redo as a small or limited amount is itself a positive cue, even in a fragment without emotion words or an explicit comparison. No need to name autosave or explain why the limited loss is fortunate.
column4: 자동 저장 덕분에 처음부터 다시 쓰지 않아도 돼서 다행이야.
column5: Luckily, autosave means I don't have to start the whole report again.
column6: 自動保存のおかげで、最初から書き直さずに済んでよかった。

column3: Accept care for the body, rest, walking or avoiding further strain. Do not demand medical reasoning. Encouraging ignoring pain and pushing through is contrary to the exercise.
column4: 무리하기 전에 몸의 신호를 알아차리고 멈춰서 다행이야.
column5: I'm glad I noticed the discomfort and stopped before pushing further.
column6: 無理をする前に体の違和感に気づいて、やめられてよかった。

column3: Accept any reasonable alternative, change of routine or opportunity after finding the cafe closed. A simple plan is enough; a named location or detailed benefit is unnecessary.
column4: 이번 기회에 골목의 새로운 카페를 가봐야겠어.
column5: This is a chance to try a new café nearby.
column6: この機会に、近くの新しいカフェへ行ってみよう。

column3: Accept a reasonable way to use the wait or constructively handle the mistaken time. An ordinary activity or a gentle next-time plan is enough.
column4: 한 시간 동안 근처를 산책하며 저녁 풍경을 구경해야겠어.
column5: I can take a walk nearby and enjoy the evening scenery.
column6: 一時間、近くを散歩して夕方の景色を楽しもう。

column3: Accept openness, curiosity, trying the unfamiliar class or another feasible way forward. The user need not promise to enjoy history or identify a specific learning outcome.
column4: 몰랐던 역사 분야를 배워보며 새로운 관심사를 찾을 기회야.
column5: This is a chance to discover an interest in a new area of history.
column6: 知らなかった歴史を学び、新しい興味を見つける機会だ。

column3: Accept a reasonable upside, adaptation or constructive response to the haircut. Mixed disappointment and acceptance are fine; do not require praising the haircut.
column4: 아직 낯설지만 머리를 말리고 손질하는 시간이 줄겠어.
column5: It feels unfamiliar, but drying and styling it will take less time.
column6: まだ慣れないけれど、乾かしたり整えたりする時間は短くなりそう。

column3: Accept own pace, enjoyment, encouragement, continued practice or learning from someone else. One gentle response to comparison is enough.
column4: 내 속도로 음악을 즐기면서 잘하는 사람에게 배울 수도 있겠어.
column5: I can enjoy music at my own pace and learn from someone more experienced.
column6: 自分のペースで音楽を楽しみながら、上手な人から学ぶこともできる。

column3: Accept any reasonable alternative, safety, rest or next step after the cancelled ferry. No need to describe an itinerary or deny disappointment; unsafe travel despite the cancellation is not constructive.
column4: 아쉽지만 안전하게 남은 제주 동네를 더 둘러볼 수 있겠어.
column5: It's disappointing, but I can safely explore another part of Jeju.
column6: 残念だけれど、安全に済州島の別の場所を見て回れそう。

column3: Accept a small social step, curiosity, a new connection or giving the unfamiliar group a chance. No explicit lesson or benefit is needed.
column4: 다른 부서 사람들을 알아가고 새로운 이야기를 들을 기회였어.
column5: It was a chance to meet coworkers and hear new perspectives.
column6: 他部署の人を知り、新しい話を聞く機会になった。

column3: Accept meaning in the spending, adjusting expectations or any reasonable next saving step. Do not require both appreciation and a budget plan.
column4: 저축은 덜 했지만 소중한 사람들을 챙겼고, 다음 달엔 경조사 예산을 따로 잡아볼래.
column5: I saved less, but cared for people who matter; next month I'll budget for these events.
column6: 貯金は少なかったけれど、大切な人を気遣えた。来月は行事の予算も作ろう。

column3: Accept trying again, a small next step, recognizing effort or any learning after rejection. Simply being willing to try again is sufficient; no detailed lesson is required.
column4: 결과는 아쉽지만 작품을 완성한 경험을 다음 작업에 살릴 수 있어.
column5: The result hurts, but I can use the experience of finishing a piece in my next project.
column6: 結果は残念だけれど、作品を完成させた経験を次に生かせる。

column3: Accept continuing applications, resting, adjusting plans, learning or recognizing effort after rejection. A simple feasible next step is enough; no detailed career strategy is required.
column4: 이번 지원 경험을 바탕으로 이력서를 다듬고 더 맞는 공고를 찾아볼래.
column5: I can use what I've learned to improve my résumé and look for roles that fit better.
column6: 今回の経験をもとに履歴書を見直し、より合う求人を探してみよう。

column3: Accept fatigue, rest, trying, limits or a gentler plan. A brief caring response is sufficient; effort and permission to rest are alternatives, not a checklist.
column4: 피곤한 몸으로 공부하러 간 것도 노력한 거야. 오늘은 쉬어도 괜찮아.
column5: Going there while tired was an effort too. It's okay to rest today.
column6: 疲れていても勉強に行ったのは頑張ったこと。今日は休んでも大丈夫。

column3: Accept different opinions, boundaries, personal pace or choosing not to internalize intrusive remarks. A short distancing phrase is enough; no explicit declaration of personal worth is required.
column4: 상대의 무례한 말이 내 가치를 정하지 않아. 내 삶은 내 속도로 살아도 돼.
column5: Their rude remarks don't define my worth. I can live at my own pace.
column6: 相手の無礼な言葉で自分の価値は決まらない。自分のペースで生きていい。

column3: Accept partial effort, imperfect consistency, kindness or simply continuing the diary. Do not require mentioning twenty days or explicitly praising past effort.
column4: 빈 날도 있지만 스무 날이나 기록한 노력은 사라지지 않아.
column5: The blank days don't erase the effort of writing on twenty days.
column6: 空白の日があっても、二十日も書いた努力は消えない。

column3: Accept partial progress, taking a break, reading later or personal pace. No need to explicitly say that half a book is meaningful.
column4: 절반을 읽은 것도 배움이야. 쉬었다가 내 속도로 이어가면 돼.
column5: Reading half was learning too. I can rest and continue at my own pace.
column6: 半分読んだことも学びだ。休んでから、自分のペースで続ければいい。

column3: Accept human fallibility, sadness without self-abuse, self-kindness or an ordinary practical next step. Do not require a statement separating possessions from personal worth.
column4: 잃어버려서 속상하지만 물건 하나 잃었다고 내가 못난 사람인 건 아니야.
column5: I'm upset about losing it, but one lost item doesn't make me a bad person.
column6: なくして悲しいけれど、物を一つなくしたからといって、だめな人間ではない。

column3: Accept endurance, effort, partial progress, realistic limits or a kind next step for the coming year. No need to list achievements or explicitly praise the year.
column4: 다 이루지는 못했지만 한 해를 살아내며 애쓴 나의 노력은 의미 있어.
column5: I didn't do everything, but the effort I put into getting through this year matters.
column6: 全部はできなかったけれど、この一年を生きて頑張った努力には意味がある。

column3: Accept any plausible external reason for the delayed reply, allowing the friend time, or recognizing the kind intention of reaching out. One contextual self-kind or non-blaming cue is enough; do not require both domains or an explicit disclaimer.
column4: 바빠서 아직 못 봤나 보다.
column5: Maybe they have been too busy to see it.
column6: 忙しくてまだ見られていないのかも。

column3: Accept unforeseeable roadworks, the reasonable choice with information available then, or a kind practical response to the delay. A single contextual cue is enough. Do not require proving the bus was objectively optimal.
column4: 공사할 줄은 몰랐지. 평소처럼 고른 거야.
column5: I could not have known about the roadworks. It was my usual choice.
column6: 工事は知らなかったし、いつもどおり選んだんだ。

column3: Accept treating this as a fixable slip, separating the mistake from worth, or a kind next step to clean the clothes. One relevant gentle cue is enough; no explicit statement of personal worth is required.
column4: 한 번 깜빡한 거지. 말리고 털면 되겠다.
column5: I forgot once. I can dry them and brush it off.
column6: 一度忘れただけ。乾かして払えばいいね。
